answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through ongoing stake instead of one-time registration. Each agent posts a bond that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, so a farm of clones pays the bond many times over while a single honest agent pays once. Like a willow that bends but holds its ground, the bond survives normal churn yet breaks under coordinated abuse; reputation then grows like a vine, branching only from verified work, and the summit of trust is reached by agents whose history is expensive to fake.
